blocks.text: Langley Farms: what the ground is and what governs it

items.t: The land base is the fact: 235 km² of the Township is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, so most Langley farm parcels are reserve land with Agricultural Land Commission housing and use rules layered over Township zoning. A specific parcel's reserve status is checked on the ALC maps by PID or civic address — never assumed from the district name.

Tenure: farm parcels are overwhelmingly freehold; strata farm product is not a Langley pattern: — no strata farm complex was confirmed on an official source, and on ALR land the form is barred outright. A Langley farm purchase is a fee-simple title purchase: Township zoning, ALR rules where the parcel is in the reserve, farm-class position, water rights and any registered covenants on title govern.

Soil capability: no agricultural capability class for the Township's main farm land was confirmed from a text source; capability is mapped per parcel in the BC Soil Information Finder, and the ALC soils page defines the classes from Class 1 (no or very slight limitations) through the lower classes. A parcel marketed on its soil class needs the per-parcel map read, not the listing's wording.

Farm classification is part of what trades: a parcel that keeps BC Assessment farm classification must keep meeting the minimum gross farm income thresholds, which scale with the size of the operation (full three-tier form).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: Zoning: Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500: applies across the Township; Township material names Rural Zones RU-1 and RU-2 and Suburban Residential Zones SR-1, SR-2 and SR-3. The minimum lot size for temporary farm labourer accommodation in Bylaw No. 2500 (s. 201.3) was not confirmed from a Township-hosted bylaw text — unconfirmed. Read the parcel's own zone section before assuming any farm or home-based use is permitted.
R-CL compact-lot frame: R-CL s.403 = 220 m² minimum lot area / 464.5 m² maximum LOT area. (Standing correction; Township Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s.403.)

Water licensing: domestic groundwater use is exempt from licensing; groundwater used for non-domestic purposes such as irrigation requires a water licence under the Water Sustainability Act, and well records are searched in the GWELLS registry. An irrigated Langley farm bought without its licence position confirmed is bought with its core input unconfirmed.

If a strata purchase is made elsewhere in Langley (redirect case): the BC strata block applies — Form B diligence; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ units since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions) — a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw. None of it applies to a Langley fee-simple farm purchase itself: no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.
The Township's SSMUH bylaw has no 6-plex tier: A Langley farm or lot priced on a 6-plex assumption is priced on a tier that does not exist in the Township bylaw.

The R-CL numbers are lot-area numbers, and one figure in circulation does not exist: R-CL s.403 sets a 220 m² minimum and a 464.5 m² maximum LOT area. There is no 355 m² figure in that section — not as a lot figure and not as a floor-area cap. (Standing correction; Township Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s.403.)

One hectare is 2.471 acres: The ALC additional-residence cap turns at 40 ha (≈98.8 acres) and the farm-class tiers at 0.8 ha and 4 ha; listings that blur the conversion blur which cap and which income tier apply to the parcel.

faq.q: How much of Langley is in the ALR?
faq.a: The Township of Langley states 235 square kilometres of the Township is within the Agricultural Land Reserve; check a specific parcel on the ALC maps.

faq.q: Can a Langley farm have a second dwelling?
faq.a: On ALR land, one additional residence is permitted without an ALC application where the conditions are met — 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or smaller, 186 m² or less on larger parcels — and Township bylaws must also permit it.

faq.q: What is the ALR and does it apply to farms in Langley?
faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is farmland protected by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission. Farm use is generally allowed on ALR land, but subdividing, adding homes or using the land for non-farm purposes usually needs approval, so check a property's ALR status before you offer.

faq.q: What should I check before buying a farm in Langley?
faq.a: Check the ALR status, water source and licences, drainage and flood history, the buildings and any quota or production licences that do or do not transfer with the land. Poultry and egg production in BC are supply-managed, so a sale of the farm does not automatically include quota.
